{{Quote|The spirits first called upon me as I lay cold and trembling, struck with a fatal affliction while birthing my first daughter.|"Wild Power," Mother Talzin|<ref name="BOS" />}}
A [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]]<ref name="Species" /> [[Gender/Legends|female]] was the '''firstborn daughter''' of [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]], [[Clan mother/Legends|matriarch]] and [[Shaman of the Nightsisters|shaman]] of the [[Witches of Dathomir]]'s [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Coven/Legends|coven]] on<ref name="BOS" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. In her religious manifesto ''[[Wild Power]]'',<ref name="BOS" /> published sometime between [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Wild Power]]'', as showcased in ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', mentions the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]''. ''Jedi Alliance'' takes place during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the beginning of which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The game must also take place before the events of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] due to the presence of [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Ziro]] within his [[Ziro's Palace/Legends|palace]]. ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film to 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], so the writing of ''Wild Power'' must have taken place afterwards. The book must also have been written prior to the [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|destruction of the Nightsisters]] as shown in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Massacre]]." {{TCWdates|419}} Therefore, Wild Power must have been written between 22 BBY and 20 BBY.</ref> Talzin claimed that while giving [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] to her [[Maul's family/Legends|daughter]], she was struck with a fatal affliction and nearly [[Death/Legends|died]]. She cited that during a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of the [[Spirit World]], she was saved by the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]]&mdash;mythological embodiments of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] in Nightsister mythology. ''Wild Power'' was one of many writings collected in the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] historical book ''[[Book of Sith]]'', assembled by [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] sometime between [[19 BBY]] and [[18 BBY]].<ref name="BOS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Talzin's firstborn daughter was mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book, ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and published by [[Chronicle Books]].<ref name="BOS" /> In his endnotes for the ''Book of Sith'', Wallace said he mapped the events of Talzin's biography, specifically the birth of her daughter, against the real-world traditions of [[Wikipedia:Shamanism|shamanism]].<ref name="BOS endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 4)}}</ref>
